audit_2026_10_29: FRESH AUDIT PASSED (first-hand, 2026-10-29) — the expansion order's fifth county, after Mecklenburg NC was SKIPPED 2026-10-23, Wake NC went live 2026-10-23, Miami-Dade FL went live 2026-10-25, and Orange FL went live 2026-10-27. (1) Layer 0 'GIS_Dashboard_Issued_CO_Merged' (Hillsborough County Accela dashboard extract, ArcGIS item b6094c69bf2c4e22b141ccdf28654dce, owner Jeff.Sanchez.hc, public access): 109,964 rows all-time; the layer MERGES two record kinds — issued-permit rows (CATEGORY='ISSUED', ISSUED_DATE set; 74,295 rows) and certificate-of-occupancy rows (CATEGORY='CO', ISSUED_DATE null, the completion carried in COMBINED_DATE; 35,669 rows). The published population is the issued rows only, defined by the ISSUED_DATE window; a permit's CO row is outside the window by definition, so no collapsing applies (verified: a sampled permit carries exactly one ISSUED row and, separately, one CO row). Layer editingInfo.dataLastEditDate 2026-10-29T11:42:33Z (same day as the audit). (2) VOLUME STABILITY measured by ISSUED_DATE year: 3,720 (2020) / 17,132 (2021) / 13,842 / 11,012 / 9,281 (2024) / 10,807 (2025) / 8,226 (2026 YTD through Oct 22) — months run 610–1,085 through 2025–2026 with no collapse of the Mecklenburg kind (the 2021 spike is the extract's early shape; recent years are steady at roughly 800–900 issued permits a month). (3) Identity measured on a full audit pull of the trailing-12-month window (ISSUED_DATE >= 2025-10-29): 9,718 rows = 9,718 distinct PERMIT__, 0 duplicates, 0 null permit numbers, and CATEGORY='ISSUED' on all 9,718 rows. (4) Coverage is county-issued permits: Hillsborough County issues permits for unincorporated Hillsborough County and county-served areas; the City of Tampa runs its own permitting system and its permits are NOT in this feed — Tampa-proper is a labeled gap on the hub (the WAVE1 audit verified Tampa publishes no usable permit feed: its one GIS layer is a 1,032-record single-family workflow extract with no valuation and no address fields). Postal cities in the window run Tampa 2,709 / Riverview 1,196 / Apollo Beach 1,098 / Wimauma 701 / Brandon 599 and the rest of the county's unincorporated communities. (5) Terms: the item's licenseInfo is the county's as-is data disclaimer (no prohibition on use; figures published 'as reported by Hillsborough County' with attribution, no endorsement implied) — the same portal-standard shape as the Miami-Dade item already live.
coverage_note: Permits issued by Hillsborough County only (unincorporated Hillsborough County and county-served areas). The City of Tampa issues its own permits through its own system and they are not in this feed; totals here are county-issued totals, labeled as such.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one PERMIT__ in the ISSUED category of Hillsborough County's merged issued/CO layer. The pull window is ISSUED_DATE, which only issued-category rows carry, so the permit's certificate-of-occupancy row (a separate layer row with ISSUED_DATE null) never enters the pull and no collapsing applies or is needed.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (ISSUED_DATE >= 2025-10-29), measured 2026-10-29 on a full audit pull: 9,718 rows = 9,718 distinct PERMIT__, 0 duplicates, 0 nulls, CATEGORY='ISSUED' on 9,718 of 9,718. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.

field_map.address: ADDRESS, as published (whitespace collapsed; all-caps values title-cased). ZIP and city come from CITY_1, the layer's single postal field ('Tampa 33625': the trailing 5-digit group is the ZIP, the rest is the postal city; a value with no ZIP group is the city alone; an empty value — or the county's own name standing in for a city on 4 window permits — names no city, so Tampa, the county seat, stands in).
field_map.application_date: The layer publishes no application-date field (its other dates are COMPLETE_DATE, the completion date on CO rows, and COMBINED_DATE, the merged issued/CO date — neither is an application date), so application_date stays NULL by construction (the Philadelphia treatment).
field_map.category: The Residential/Commercial prefix of TYPE, the county's own permit naming: Residential 7,857 window permits / Commercial 1,861 — every window TYPE carries one of the two prefixes.
field_map.contractor_rule: NONE CARRIED — the layer's full 25-field schema publishes no owner, applicant, or contractor name field at all (verified against the layer metadata, 2026-10-29). contractor_name stays NULL, never inferred (the Philadelphia treatment).
field_map.issue_date: ISSUED_DATE (epoch ms in the ArcGIS feed, converted to the civil date). The window is defined on it: a record enters this report when the county records an issue date.
field_map.permit_number: PERMIT__ (unique in the window, see dedupe_rule).
field_map.permit_type: TYPE, the county's own family naming (Residential New Construction, Commercial Miscellaneous, ...). The county's family code drives the trade classification together with the scope text (see trades.classify_hillsborough_trade: the source-named New Construction family wins first; the scope is mined only for strong signals — signage, re-roof, HVAC and the like — and pools, screen enclosures, sheds, additions, and renovations stay general).
field_map.status: STATUS_1, the permit's current status, mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source. Window statuses: Complete 5,039 / Issued 3,430 (incl. 7 stated 'ISSUED') / In Process 611 / Expired 254 / About to Expire 169 / Awaiting Client Reply 141 / Revision 66 / Pending 7 / Exempt 1 — every window record carries an issue date, so post-issuance states stay in the population (the Raleigh treatment).
field_map.valuation: Value FAILED validation on the full window (measured 2026-10-29) and is NOT carried: valuation stays NULL and Hillsborough publishes counts only. Evidence: stated on 9,706 of 9,718 permits (12 null, 14 at $0, only 2 at $1, median $50,000 — the bulk of the field looks sane), but (a) a project's figure is restated identically on the project's separate permits: one county lift-station project states $69,000,000 on each of two permits at the same address (the second permit's own scope calls itself 'permit 2 of 3 for this specific project'), and a two-building apartment project states $34,857,000 on each building's permit; and (b) standalone values are corrupted at the top end for ordinary homes: a 4,072 sq ft single-family house states $98,975,000 and a 3,144 sq ft single-family house states $95,025,000 (roughly $24,000–$30,000 per square foot of living area), with further single-family permits at $23,000,000 and a foundation-only single-family permit at $15,000,000. Values above $10M alone total $1,108,945,047 of the $2,832,162,238.01 raw window sum (39.2%), so the total is built on the least trustworthy slice. No trustworthy aggregate exists, so per the Austin/Miami-Dade precedent the pages ship without any dollar figure and the reason is stated on the Data Sources page. The raw field stays in the vault (it is in pull_select) as reported, unpublished, and is re-validated only if the source's field changes character.

history_range: ISSUED_DATE 2019 onward in the source (109,964 merged issued+CO rows; 74,295 issued rows); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).
license: Hillsborough County as-is data disclaimer (named in the ArcGIS item's licenseInfo); attribution: Hillsborough County, Florida
order_sql: ISSUED_DATE ASC, PERMIT__ ASC, OBJECTID ASC
rate_limit: ArcGIS hosted FeatureServer query, 2,000-row pages (the layer's maxRecordCount) with the adapter's 0.4s pacing plus retries; anonymous public tier served the full audit and backfill pulls steadily.
source_name: Hillsborough County open data — Accela issued permits dashboard extract
terms_status: verified-open-2026-10-29: the ArcGIS item record for 'AccelaDashBoard_MapService20211019' (publisher: Hillsborough County; owner Jeff.Sanchez.hc; access public) carries the county's as-is disclaimer in licenseInfo and no restriction on reuse; figures are published 'as reported by Hillsborough County' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: Daily (county Accela dashboard extract); MEASURED 2026-10-29: layer dataLastEditDate 2026-10-29T11:42:33Z (same day) and newest ISSUED_DATE 2026-10-22. Freshness (gate 5) is measured as the layer's editingInfo.dataLastEditDate under a 96h threshold. Risk noted in the WAVE1 audit: the feed is a dashboard extract whose refresh is the county's choice — the max issue date is re-verified at every refresh and the freshness gate holds the county if the extract goes silent.
watermark_field: ISSUED_DATE + PERMIT__ — refresh re-pulls by the ISSUED_DATE watermark and upserts.
